meta.title: Well-regarded sitcoms since 1970

scope.years: Premiered 1969 or later (The Brady Bunch, September 1969, is the one 1969 premiere)
scope.kinds: Sitcoms, dramedies that competed as comedies, a few sketch-adjacent shows from the IMDb list

inclusion_reasons.imdb-list: On the IMDb user list 'All '80s-'90s American 22-minute sitcoms with at least 1,000 votes' (ls080851026), captured 2026-10-19
inclusion_reasons.emmy-comedy-winner: Won the Primetime Emmy for Outstanding Comedy Series. Every winner from 1971 through 2026 is included.
inclusion_reasons.golden-globe-comedy-winner: Won the Golden Globe for Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy. Every winner from 1971 through 2026 is included except the ones in excluded_award_winners.
inclusion_reasons.curated-newer: Popular or acclaimed sitcom from 1998 on
inclusion_reasons.curated-animated: Well-regarded animated comedy (Emmy winner, long run or strong critical standing)
inclusion_reasons.curated-international: Well-regarded English-language sitcom made outside the US
inclusion_reasons.curated-dramedy: Well-regarded dramedy, or an award winner the other lists missed

emmy_outstanding_comedy_series.1970: My World and Welcome to It (premiered 1969)

field_notes.id: Stable key: slug of the title plus first premiere year. Matches the tracker's rating keys.
field_notes.imdb_id: Filled for the 155 IMDb-list shows; null elsewhere until enriched (see scripts/enrich_imdb.py).
field_notes.status: running, ended, or uncertain (a recent revival or special with no announced future)
field_notes.years: Overall span across all runs; end is null while running
field_notes.runs: Each original run or revival with its networks in broadcast order and its season count when known
field_notes.seasons: Total seasons (series, for British shows); specials are noted rather than counted
field_notes.creators_stars: Keys into the people table. IMDb person IDs where the IMDb list supplied them, otherwise p-<name>
field_notes.labels: Editorial: ratings-hit (big original audience), critics-favorite, cult-favorite, streaming-hit. May be empty.
field_notes.awards: Year is the ceremony year. Golden Globe years were converted from the season year shown on Wikipedia's winners list to the following January's ceremony.
field_notes.tags: humor and tone are weighted 3 (defining), 2 (strong), 1 (present); the weights come from tag order in the original tagging pass and are meant to be edited. Other categories are plain lists.
field_notes.imdb_list: Snapshot from the IMDb list as captured; rating and votes are rounded as IMDb displayed them
field_notes.checked: Present when status and season count were checked against news sources on the given date
field_notes.derived: Computed by the build script; do not edit by hand

provenance.from_imdb_list: title, imdb_id, imdb_list.*, creators and stars (with IMDb person IDs) for the 155 list shows
provenance.checked_online: awards (Wikipedia winners lists, 2026-10-26); status of shows still running or recently revived (news sources, October 2026)
provenance.editorial_unverified: networks, runs and season counts for most shows, cast and creators for shows not on the IMDb list, labels, tags, notes

data_issues: Barbara Weisberg has two IMDb IDs (nm6722400, nm2462619) on Charles in Charge; kept the first
Charles in Charge: duplicate credit for Barbara Weisberg removed

format.multi-cam: Filmed on a stage before a studio audience (or with a laugh track); classic sitcom look and rhythm
format.single-cam: Shot like a film, usually without a laugh track; more cinematic and quieter
format.single-cam-laugh-track: Shot like a film but with a laugh track added
format.sketch-variety: Sketches and musical bits rather than one continuing story

devices.fourth-wall: Characters talk directly to the viewer
devices.meta: Jokes about being a TV show or about TV itself
devices.musical-numbers: Songs or performances built into episodes
devices.live-episodes: Some episodes performed and broadcast live
devices.multi-role-star: The lead plays several different characters
devices.stylized-visuals: Unusual camera work, graphics or visual gags
devices.show-within-show: Follows the making of a fictional TV program
devices.mockumentary: Shot like a documentary, with talking-head interviews
devices.talking-animals: Animal characters who talk and act like people

humor.insult: Put-downs and roasting as a main engine
humor.absurdist: Illogical or ridiculous situations played straight
humor.satire: Targets institutions, politics, media or society
humor.parody: Spoofs a genre or other media
humor.dark: Finds comedy in bleak or taboo subjects
humor.topical: References to current events of its day
humor.schemes: Get-rich-quick plans and plots that backfire

tone.warm: Characters basically like each other; affectionate
tone.very-special-episodes: Periodic serious issue episodes with a lesson
tone.heartfelt: Real emotional stakes alongside the jokes
tone.cynical: Selfish or jaded characters; little sentiment
tone.mean-spirited: Characters are cruel to each other as the main joke
tone.socially-conscious: Engages with race, class, gender, politics or war
tone.nostalgic: Looks back fondly at an earlier era

setting.home: Family home is the main set
setting.workplace: Job site is a main set
setting.media: TV, radio, magazine, newspaper or publishing
setting.period-historical: Set in an earlier century or a historical era

themes.parenting: Raising kids from the parents' view
themes.nanny-housekeeper: Live-in help as a lead character
themes.fish-out-of-water: Someone thrown into an unfamiliar world
themes.career-woman: A woman's professional ambitions at the center
themes.race-culture: Race and cultural identity explored directly
themes.addiction-recovery: Recovery from alcohol or drug addiction
themes.mental-illness: Mental illness as part of the premise
themes.creature: Robot, monster or creature as a main character
themes.genre-spoof: Parodies a cop, spy or soap genre
themes.mystery: A mystery to solve drives the story
themes.teacher-mentor: Teacher or mentor guiding young people
themes.nostalgia: Built on looking back at the past
themes.comedian-vehicle: Built around a stand-up comic's persona

structure.episodic: Self-contained episodes; watch in any order
structure.mixed: Mostly standalone with ongoing relationship arcs

content.mature: Cable-level language, sex or dark content

cast.black-led: Black lead or predominantly Black cast
